([[Gaithersburg, Maryland]]) | college = [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross]] (2011–2015) | draft_year = 2015 | career_start = 2015 | years1 = 2015–2016 | team1 = [[Maine Red Claws]] | years2 = 2016–2017 | team2 = [[Alba Berlin]] | years3 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2019|end}} | team3 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years4 = [[2017–18 NBA G League season|2017]]–[[2018–19 NBA G League season|2019]] | team4 = →[[Raptors 905]] | years5 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2020–2021]] | team5 = [[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years6 = 2021–2022 | team6 = [[Vanoli Cremona]] | years7 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]] | team7 = Raptors 905 | years8 = 2022 | team8 = [[Formosa Taishin Dreamers]] | years9 = 2023 | team9 = [[Limoges CSP]] | years10 = 2023–2024 | team10 = [[Unione Cestistica Casalpusterlengo]] | years11 = 2024–2025 | team11 = [[Taipei Taishin Mars]] | years12 = 2025–present | team12 = [[Taoyuan Taiwan Beer Leopards]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2019 NBA Finals|2019]]) * Second-team All-[[Patriot League]] (2015) * 2× [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League|TPBL]] All-Defensive Second Team ([[2024–25 TPBL season|2025]], [[2025–26 TPBL season|2026]]) * Third-team All-Patriot League (2014) }} '''Malcolm Miller''' (born March 6, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Taoyuan Taiwan Beer Leopards]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross Crusaders]]. Miller has played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Toronto Raptors]], whom he won a [[NBA Championship|championship]] with in [[2019 NBA Finals|2019]]. ==High school career== Miller attended [[Gaithersburg High School]] where he served as team captain during both his junior and senior seasons, averaging 13.1 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 2.6 blocks and 1.4 steals per game as a senior, earning him first team All-Gazette honors.{{cite web|url=http://www.goholycross.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=33100&ATCLID=210214022|title=Holy Cross bio|work=GoHolyCross.com|access-date=October 10, 2015}} ==College career== In four years at [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross]], Miller totaled 1,013 points, 532 rebounds, 164 assists, 143 blocked shots and 93 steals, ranking third all-time in career blocked shots and sixth in career games started (93).{{cite web|url=http://www.goholycross.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=33100&SPID=157228&ATCLID=210369803&KEY=|title=Malcolm Miller Added To Boston Celtics Training Camp Roster|work=GoHolyCross.com|date=September 25, 2015|access-date=October 10, 2015}} As a senior, Miller averaged 14.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.6 blocked shots, 1.3 steals and 1.2 assists per game for the Crusaders, while connecting on 37.2 percent of his three-point field goal attempts and 83.0 percent of his free throws. He finished the season ranked second in the [[Patriot League men's basketball tournament|Patriot League]] in blocked shots, fourth in free throw percentage, seventh in steals, eighth in scoring, 14th in three-point field goals made and 15th in rebounding. Miller led the team in scoring 13 times and in rebounding 13 times that year, while scoring in double-figures 25 times. ==Professional career== ===Maine Red Claws (2015–2016)=== After going undrafted on the [[2015 NBA draft]], Miller joined the [[Boston Celtics]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-announce-2015-summer-league-roster|title=Celtics Announce 2015 Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2015|access-date=October 10, 2015}} where he averaged 4.0 points and 1.3 rebounds in 12.1 minutes per game. On September 25, 2015, he signed with the Celtics.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-finalize-training-camp-roster-0|title=Celtics Finalize Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2015|access-date=October 10, 2015}} However, he was later waived by the Celtics on October 20 after appearing in one preseason game.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-waive-three|title=Celtics Waive Three|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2015|access-date=October 20, 2015}} On October 31, he was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Celtics.{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065518|title=Red Claws Announce Draft Results, Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015}} ===Alba Berlin (2016–2017)=== On July 27, 2016, Miller signed with [[Alba Berlin]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] and EuroCup.{{cite news|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/75ptv6l6vnjqmmk9/alba-signs-athletic-forward-miller|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160804215201/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/75ptv6l6vnjqmmk9/alba-signs-athletic-forward-miller|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 4, 2016|title=ALBA signs athletic forward Miller|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 27, 2016|access-date=July 29, 2016}} ===Toronto Raptors (2017–2020)=== For the 2017–18 season, Miller signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the NBA as the team's first [[two-way contract]] recipient. He would spend most of the season with the Raptors' G-League affiliate [[Raptors 905]].{{cite news|first=Doug|last=Smith|title=Raptors ink Malcolm Miller to team's first two-way contract |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/2017/07/06/raptors-ink-malcolm-miller-to-teams-first-two-way-contract.html|work=[[Toronto Star]]|date=July 6, 2017|access-date=July 8, 2017}} Miller would play in 15 NBA regular season games for the Raptors, starting four times. He made his first career NBA start on March 4, 2018, against the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. On February 10, 2019, Miller re-signed with the Toronto Raptors as a part of the main roster.{{cite web|title=Raptors Sign Miller|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-malcolm-miller|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 11, 2019|date=February 10, 2019}} That season, Miller played in 10 playoff games and won a championship with Raptors after they defeated the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2019 NBA Finals]]. In the 2019–20 season, Miller played in 28 games for the Raptors, starting once. ===Salt Lake City Stars (2021)=== On December 18, 2020, Miller signed a contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-yogi-ferrell-and-malcolm-miller|title=Jazz Sign Yogi Ferrell and Malcolm Miller|work=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2020|access-date=December 19, 2020}} He
